---
title: "Building and testing"
---

## Build

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fre-ms/zotLook.git
cd zotLook
./build.sh
```

`build.sh` compiles the helper binary (`qlpreview`) for both architectures and
signs them — `swiftc` ad-hoc signs the arm64 slice but not the x86_64 one, and
`lipo` does not sign the container, so without this the result reports as
unsigned. It then packages the `.xpi` and rewrites `update.json` to match:
version, download URL and SHA-256 all derived from the manifest and the file
that was just built.

A release build therefore needs **macOS with the Xcode Command Line Tools**.
That helper is the only compiled piece in the package: the Windows route drives
QuickLook's pipe through js-ctypes and ships no binary of its own.

The same script also runs on **Linux**, where there is no Swift toolchain. It
packages everything else, which is all the Linux route needs, and leaves
`update.json` alone — a package without the helper is fine to install and test
locally, but publishing its checksum would auto-update macOS copies to a build
that has lost their Quick Look panel.

## Repository layout

```
addon/     copied verbatim into the XPI; the plugin as Zotero sees it
native/    Swift helpers, compiled by build.sh rather than shipped
asset/     images
doc/       this documentation
test/      test suite
build/     the packaged .xpi; git-ignored
```

Zotero requires `manifest.json`, `bootstrap.js` and `locale/` at the **root** of
the XPI, which is why `addon/` is packaged from its inside rather than as a
folder.

`update.json` stays at the repository root rather than moving into `build/`: it
is not a build artefact but a published file, and its URL on `main` is what
installed copies poll.

## Tests

```bash
npm install   # linkedom, to stand in for Gecko's DOM, and eslint
npm test      # lints first, then runs the suites
```

::: {.callout-important title="The lint step is not decoration"}
A lost function parameter leaves an identifier that still parses but throws at
runtime. `node --check` cannot see it, and every suite missed it for as long as
the function around it was stubbed.
:::

The suites run the plugin's own source in a scope with Zotero's sandbox globals
stubbed, so the parsing, sanitising, keyboard, menu and EPUB code can be
exercised without launching Zotero. Rendering is driven through a stand-in
worker that speaks the same two-step protocol the real one does.

They also check the things that otherwise fail silently: that `update.json`
agrees with the manifest, that both locale bundles define exactly the strings
the code asks for, and that the renderer's source still carries every
requirement pdf.js imposes on it — each of which was found by watching it fail,
and none of which announces itself when it is missing.

The plugin has no runtime dependencies; `linkedom` is a development dependency
only and is never packaged.

## CI

Runs on every push and pull request.

The suites run on **Linux**, where they are platform-independent, and on
**Windows**, where a pathname is not a path and the assumptions differ. The
release build runs on **macOS**, because `swiftc`, `lipo` and `codesign` live
only there; it checks that the XPI holds every file Zotero needs at its root and
that the helper is universal and signed. The suites run a second time on that
job, where a freshly built XPI is present, so the check that `update.json`
describes the file that was actually produced also runs.

The XPI is not byte-reproducible — zip records modification times — so CI does
not compare its checksum against the committed `update.json`. What it does
compare is the version, which is what actually goes stale.

## This documentation

```bash
cd doc && ./build.sh
python3 doc/offline/smoketest.py site/en site/de
```

Both language projects render into `site/{en,de}`, the offline repairs are
applied, and one linked PDF per language is built with Typst.

The site is built on the
[zotqda-quarto-theme](https://github.com/fre-ms/zotqda-quarto-theme), which is
**vendored** into `doc/_theme/` so the documentation builds without a sibling
checkout. `doc/update-theme.sh` pulls a newer copy in.

Quarto is pinned, and the pin is the one the other ecosystem sites use, so they
all render on the same version. Upgrades are deliberate: build with
`ALLOW_UNPINNED_QUARTO=1`, run the smoke test, look at a page, then move the
pin.

The sidebars of the two languages must stay **parallel** — `gen_langmap.py`
derives the language switcher's page-to-page map from them, and fails the build
if they stop matching.
